messages.subject: Including covariates with formula=~ ..
parts:
Hello, 

I'm working on distance sampling with R to estimate abundance and density of a bird population. My study uses the point transect method. 
Data contain observation point data of 10 years in 2 different regions (Region.Label) 

My data used for DS contain the following columns
"Region.Label" (South or East), "Sample.Label" (ID of the observation point), "Effort", "distance", "Area", "size", "year", "Point", "Xcoord", "Ycoord" (coordinates of latitude and longitude).

I tests different model for the Detection function. 
For the first 2 models, it works well:
mod1 <- ds(DSdata, truncation = list(left=0, right=3.1), transect = "point", formula=~Region.Label, key = "hn")
mod2 <- ds(DSdata, truncation = list(left=0, right=3.1), transect = "point", formula=~Region.Label+year, key = "hn")

I would like to know how can i integrate covariate's interaction in my model. 
Usually, in R, for some different model (not in distance sampling) I write it like that:  Region.Label*Year, or Region.Label+Year+ Region.Label*Year or Region.Label:Year.

But when I try this: 
mod3 <- ds(DSdata, truncation = list(left=0, right=3.1), transect = "point", formula=~Region.Label*year, key = "hn")
No models could be fitted. 

It is a writing problem of "formula=" ?
I don't know how to solve this problem. 

Thank you for your help and feedback,

sorry for my english i hope you'll understand the sense of my SOS.


Alice

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Including covariates with formula=~ ..
parts:
Alice

I don't know about the quantity of data you have, but I suspect the message you received is not an error message, but rather because the job of fitting a detection function to your data is actually too difficult.  The notation you have provided is correct, so that is not the problem.

The model you have requested (with strata and year as interacting covariates) is asking that a 20 parameter detection function be fitted.  I suspect there are one or more of the stratum/year combinations you have few data and this is causing model fitting challenges for the software.

Given your data are in R, you can do a quick tablulation of how many data you have to fit a model with as many parameters as these.  You note that you can fit a model with simply stratum (10 parameters) or stratum+year (11 parameters) the software succeeds in producing detection function parameter estimates, but with the most complex model, the challenge is too great.

I hope this answers your question.
